configuration.value: two transonic inlet stages + six subsonic stages, no inlet guide vanes, exit guide vanes
configuration.quote: This compressor consisted of two transonic inlet stages and six subsonic stages designed to produce an over-all total-pressure ratio of 10.26 ... The transonic inlet stage was designed without guide vanes for an axial inlet and a maximum relative Mach number of 1.20.

tip_diameter.quote: The tip diameter of the compressor was 20 inches and the inlet hub-tip ratio at the entrance to the first rotor was 0.48.

tip_radius_fixed.quote: the tip radius was fixed by the casing of the compressor of reference 4 at 10 inches, and the hub radius entering the first rotor could not be reduced below 4.8 inches because of the existing inlet bearing support geometry.

inlet_hub_tip_ratio.quote: the inlet hub-tip ratio at the entrance to the first rotor was 0.48.

design_total_pressure_ratio.quote: designed to produce an over-all total-pressure ratio of 10.26 with a mass flow of 29.8 pounds per square feet of rotor frontal area at a tip speed of 1168 feet per second.

transonic_stages_design_values.quote: Axial Mach number entering first rotor . . . 0.534; Total-pressure ratio across transonic stages . . . 1.888; Equivalent weight flow, lb/sec . . . 65; Equivalent weight flow per unit rotor frontal area, (lb/sec)/sq ft . . . 29.8; Equivalent tip speed, ft/sec . . . 1168

transonic_stage_pressure_ratio_and_effic.quote: an assumed polytropic efficiency of 0.88 for the transonic stages and with the relative Mach number entering the first rotor at the tip limited to 1.20 ... The total-pressure ratio was divided between the two stages with each having a total-pressure ratio of 1.374.

gamma.quote: γ ratio of specific heats, cp/cv, 1.3947

angle_convention.value: β angle between absolute velocity vector and rotor axis; β' angle between relative velocity vector and rotor axis; ψ angle between blade chord and compressor axis; φ camber angle of circular-arc section (included angle of mean line)
angle_convention.quote: β angle between absolute velocity vector and rotor axis, deg; β' angle between relative velocity vector and rotor axis, deg; ... φ camber angle of circular-arc blade section (included angle of mean line), deg; ψ angle between blade chord and compressor axis, deg

station_numbering.value: 1,3,5,...,15 ahead of rotors of stages 1-8; 2,4,6,...,16 ahead of stators of stages 1-8; 20 discharge measuring station
station_numbering.quote: 1,3,5, . . . 15 stations ahead of rotor of 1st, 2nd, 3rd, . . . 8th stages; 2,4,6, . . . 16 stations ahead of stator of 1st, 2nd, 3rd, . . . 8th stages; 20 discharge measuring station

transonic_rotor_profile.value: circular-arc mean line with circular-arc pressure and suction surfaces (double circular arc type), LE/TE radius 0.020 in.
transonic_rotor_profile.quote: The blade sections used for the transonic rotor blades were composed of circular-arc pressure and suction surfaces and had a circular-arc mean line. ... A leading- and trailing-edge radius of 0.020 inch was used for all sections.

transonic_rotor_incidence_and_deviation_.quote: An assumed incidence angle of 4° was used for all blade sections. ... The deviation-angle rule used, obtained from preliminary single-transonic-stage data, was δ° = 0.475φ/σ ... φ = (Δβ' - i)/(1 - 0.475/σ)

transonic_rotor1_thickness.value: 9.5 percent chord at hub to 5 percent at tip, approximately parabolic
transonic_rotor1_thickness.quote: The maximum blade thickness of the first rotor was varied from 9.5 percent of chord at the hub to 5 percent at the tip in an approximate parabolic distribution in order to reduce the blade stresses at the root.

transonic_rotor_sections_and_stacking.value: sections on five meridional streamline surfaces of revolution through area centres of equal-area increments; stacked on a radial line through approximate section centres of gravity
transonic_rotor_sections_and_stacking.quote: Blade-section profiles were thus determined along five meridional streamline surfaces of revolution. These streamlines were assumed to pass through area centers of equal-area increments. The five sections were then stacked about a radial line passing through the approximate center of gravity of each section

transonic_rotor1_solidity_intent.quote: a solidity of approximately 1.2 at the tip and 1.88 at the hub was used for the first rotor. The high tip solidity necessitated a larger chord at the tip than at the hub.

transonic_stator_profile.quote: The stator blades for the transonic stages used 65-series blower blade sections since all Mach numbers entering these stators were below 0.80

subsonic_profile.value: NACA 65-series blower blade sections, chosen at the cascade design point from ref. 10 (NACA RM L51G31) charts; constant camber (mean-radius value) for stators 6, 7, 8 and exit vanes
subsonic_profile.quote: NACA 65-series blower blade sections were used for all subsonic blading ... In the case of the sixth, seventh, and eighth stator and exit vanes, the design-point cambers varied so little from hub to tip that a constant camber blade was used; the mean-radius design-point camber was used over the blade height.

subsonic_angles_effective.value: Table II angles for subsonic stages are 'effective angles' based on average axial velocity across a blade row; transonic-stage angles are actual angles
subsonic_angles_effective.quote: The values of inlet air angle and turning angle given in table II for the subsonic stages are "effective angles" (fig. 3(b) of ref. 4) based on the average axial velocity across a blade row. The angles given for the transonic stages are actual angles.

straight_through_selection.value: subsonic blade sections chosen on a straight-through basis (turning = difference of inlet and outlet angle at same radius)
straight_through_selection.quote: All subsonic blade sections were chosen on a "straight-through" basis; that is, the turning angle was the difference between the inlet and the outlet air angle at the same radius.

stator_thickness.quote: The stator blades were made 6-percent thick at all radii

subsonic_rotor_chord.value: constant chord; thickness varied hub to tip (table III)
subsonic_rotor_chord.quote: The rotor blades were of constant chord length and the thickness varied from hub to tip (table III).

boundary_layer_allowance.value: hub radii decreased by estimated displacement thickness of combined wall boundary layers; zero at rotor 1 inlet, linear increase through stage 4, constant after (fig. 2)
boundary_layer_allowance.quote: This distribution assumed a zero thickness at the inlet to the first rotor, a linearly increasing thickness through the fourth stage, and a constant thickness for the remaining stages.

exit_guide_vanes.value: a row of exit guide vanes removes swirl leaving the last stator (no geometry tabulated)
exit_guide_vanes.quote: The tangential velocity component leaving the last-stage stators was removed by a row of exit guide vanes in order to have axial discharge from the compressor.

modified_casing.quote: the internal casing diameter at the entrance of the seventh stage (station 7, fig. 2) was held at 20.00 inches, and the diameter at the entrance of the first stage (station 1, fig. 2) was increased to 20.86 inches. From the entrance of the first stage to the entrance of the seventh stage, the internal casing diameter was decreased linearly from 20.86 to 20.00 inches.

modified_design_point.quote: Over-all total-pressure ratio . . . 10.26; Weight flow per unit rotor frontal area, (lb/sec)/sq ft . . . 30.5; Wheel speed, rpm . . . 13,380; Over-all adiabatic efficiency . . . 0.86

modified_inlet.quote: The increase in the inlet tip diameter resulted in a first-stage design tip speed of 1218 feet per second, a maximum relative tip Mach number of 1.25, and an inlet hub-tip ratio of 0.46.

modified_blading.value: same aerodynamic blading as RM E53I24 except blade twist, thickness and camber variations extrapolated to lengthen blades of stages 1-6, and larger base fillets (0.12 in. last five stages, 0.18 in. faired 0.5 in. up in first three stages; original 0.06 in.)
modified_blading.quote: The aerodynamic configuration of the compressor blading is the same as that used in the compressor of reference 1, except that (1) blade twist, thickness, and camber variations were extrapolated to facilitate lengthening the blades as required by the increase in the flow passage area from the first through the sixth stages, and (2) blade base fillets were enlarged

hub_curvature_change.value: rate of change of hub curvature through stages 1 and 2 reduced (location shown in fig. 2 only)
hub_curvature_change.quote: the rate of change of hub curvature through the first and second stages was reduced to the minimum that was compatible with strength requirements in the second-stage rotor disk.

stator_reset_earlier_phase.value: several stator rows were reset after the original tests; the reset angles are not given in RM E55B28 and that blading was destroyed by a fatigue failure
stator_reset_earlier_phase.quote: The blade angles of several of the stator rows were reset in an attempt to improve the design-speed performance, and the investigation of the compressor was continued. During this phase of the investigation, a fatigue failure in one or more of the blade rows resulted in complete destruction of all compressor blading.
